brief: BTIG's technical note argues that beneath a resilient S&P 500, internal deterioration is building. NYSE downside volume (20-day average) has surged to 54% of total volume, near year-to-date highs, while SPX is about 3% below its high (versus roughly 9% off in March) and small-caps (RTY) are down 7% (versus an 11% drawdown in March). This combination has occurred 12 times since 1996, near cycle tops including March 2000, November 2007, and November 2021. Forward SPX returns after past occurrences are mixed, but RTY's average and median 40-day returns are both -2.1%. The note ties this to credit: CCC spreads have widened above 9% (widest since 2023) and more than 6 points over B-rated spreads, a level BTIG says has historically coincided with meaningful drawdowns, and are now wider than during the 2022 bear market. Small-caps' underperformance against large-caps is framed as a reaction to this credit widening. The note flags a peak in consumer high-versus-low-quality performance, recommending a move up in quality, and put/call ratios near year-to-date lows, meaning little fear is priced in. Separately, it turns bullish on Bitcoin, seeing a target of 82k and then roughly 90k as long as 75k holds after last week's reversal.
